content: The document outlines a comprehensive framework for addressing health inequities, gender disparities, and discrimination through strategic planning, technical assistance, and stakeholder engagement. It emphasizes the importance of analyzing national health policies, strategies, and plans to identify gaps and prioritize actions that align with Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and the WHO’s General Programme of Work (GPW 13). Key elements include: 1. Reducing Inequities: Strategic documents are analyzed to propose actions and interventions aimed at reducing gender and health inequities, as well as discrimination. Stakeholder participation is assessed in the design, implementation, and evaluation of interventions to reduce health disparities. 2. Accountability for Gender, Equity, and Rights (GER) Mainstreaming: National capacities are built to integrate gender, equity, and human rights into health systems, ensuring sustainability in implementing the Country Cooperation Strategy (CCS). The CCS aligns with GPW 13’s triple billion targets, which aim to achieve universal health coverage (UHC), protect populations from health emergencies, and promote healthier populations by 2023. 3. Health Indicators and Data Analysis: Health indicators, including the top causes of death and disease burden, are reviewed to reveal inequities and gender-related issues. Trend analyses and projections of disease burden are prepared to identify progress and future challenges. Key indicators are spotlighted in the CCS, with root causes and country-level actions identified to address them. 4. Triple Billion Targets: The triple billion targets include: 1 billion more people benefiting from UHC. 1 billion more people better protected from health emergencies. 1 billion more people enjoying better health and well-being. 5. Universal Health Coverage (UHC): Countries prioritize UHC-related indicators based on their context, focusing on essential services and financial protection. 6. Health Emergencies: The goal is to protect 1 billion more people from health emergencies by improving preparedness, prevention, and response. Strategic priorities for fragile or disaster-prone countries include addressing acute events, disease outbreaks, and natural or human-induced disasters. 7. Healthier Populations: This target addresses determinants of health outside the direct control of the health sector, requiring multisectoral action, legislation, and policy. 8. National Health and Development Agenda: Analysis includes examining national health policies, financing, governance, and SDG targets to identify gaps and align priorities. 9. Partnerships and Collaboration: The role of current and potential partners is analyzed to support government health priorities. Opportunities for collaboration with UN agencies and other stakeholders are explored to promote a whole-of-government approach to health. 10. Global Action Plan for Healthy Lives and Well-being for All: This plan emphasizes joint action among multilateral health organizations to accelerate progress on health-related SDGs. It includes commitments to engage with countries, align operational strategies, and enhance accountability through shared learning. The CCS serves as a joint WHO-Member State instrument to implement GPW 13, aligning with national needs and priorities while leveraging partnerships and resources to achieve health equity and sustainable development.
